claims.text: What it = good for US finds superfic growths, incl in the breasts
claims.quote: Ultrasound can identify superficial growths and foreign bodies (eg, in the thyroid gland, breasts, testes, limbs, and some lymph nodes).

claims.text: Sx or a palpable lump: breast US = USU the first test; if it = abnorm or unclear, mammography follows; if imaging suggests CA, bx
claims.quote: Patients who present with breast symptoms (eg, pain, nipple discharge) or a palpable breast mass or other abnormality (eg, skin lesions) on clinical breast examination are typically evaluated initially with breast ultrasound. If ultrasound results are abnormal or indeterminate, mammography is performed. If imaging findings suggest cancer, biopsy is performed.

claims.text: Cyst or solid? The first question = cystic versus solid, b/c cysts are rarely CA; US USU decides this
claims.quote: Initially, physicians try to differentiate solid from cystic masses because cysts are rarely cancerous. Typically, this is determined with breast ultrasound

claims.text: Lesions that look cystic may be aspirated, for ex when they cause Sx
claims.quote: Lesions that appear cystic may be aspirated (eg, when they cause symptoms).

claims.text: After other imaging An abnorm breast MRI = USU followed by US to decide whether to bx, and under which guidance
claims.quote: An abnormal breast MRI is typically evaluated with ultrasound to determine whether biopsy should be performed under guidance with ultrasound or MRI.
